newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-ZAHID GIVES NEW ZEALAND ROUGH RECEPTION.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ZAHID GIVES NEW ZEALAND ROUGH RECEPTION.

text.p: Young Pakistan paceman Mohammad Zahid ripped New Zealand apart in their opening tour match when he took six for 54 as the visitors were bundled out for a meagre 171 on the first day of their three-day match against a Pakistan Cricket Board XI on Sunday.

The 20-year-old, playing before his home crowd, enhanced his claims for a place in the first test later this week with an impressive 19-over spell on a difficult pitch after the Kiwis acting captain Mark Greatbatch won the toss and chose to bat.
New Zealand struck back in the final session to leave the Board XI on 32 for two when bad light ended play five overs early.
Danny Morrison removed opener Shadab Kabir and night-watchman Mohammad Hussain with successive deliveries and at the close Zahoor Elahi was on 22 and Sohail Jaffar three.
Only opener Bryan Young and Stephen Fleming played the Pakistan bowling with any confidence, Young top-scoring with 47, which included four fours from 128 balls, while left-hander Fleming made 30.
The pair shared a third-wicket stand of 63 in 144 balls after Craig Spearman and Adam Parore had fallen cheaply.
New Zealand struggled to 54 for two at lunch but lost five wickets in the afternoon session and were 136 for seven at tea.
Matthew Hart, going in at number nine, contributed a valuable 22, the third highest score of the innings, before he was yorked by Zahid.
Left-arm spinner Mohammad Hussain took two for 39 and off-spinner Murtaza Hussain two for 45.
